title: Advanced Ski Program
goal: Stronger ankles. More control. Less fatigue. Bigger days on snow.

principles.title: Use your core, not your lower back.

dailyBasics.title: Stable Ankles
dailyBasics.text: Absorb terrain and stay in control.

dailyBasics.title: Ski-Ready Movement
dailyBasics.text: Confidence and endurance for the slopes.

overview.focus: Week 1 introduces advanced movement patterns with single-leg power, explosive jumping, off-balance loading, and dynamic stability while maintaining essential ankle and knee mobility.
Week 2 increases intensity with more dynamic single-leg work, reactive landing and off-balance loads. Build explosive strength, control and resilience for the demands of the mountain.

Week 3 builds explosive strength, faster transition control, and off-balance power with more dynamic single-leg work, cable resistance, and multi-planar movement. You'll move more athletically and stay stable under load.

Week 4 builds higher force and complexity with off-balance loading, single-leg strength, and reactive power. You'll increase intensity, improve multi-planar control, and develop the ability to absorb and redirect force in unpredictable terrain.

Week 5 increases intensity with higher height jumps, more complex off-balance loads, unilateral plyometrics, and multi-directional control. You'll build power endurance and confidence in unpredictable terrain.

Week 6 focuses on high-intensity power, maximal single-leg control, complex movement patterns, and ski-specific endurance. You will move faster, react quicker, and stay stable in dynamic, unpredictable terrain.

Week 7 peaks your intensity with high-demand single-leg power, complex movement patterns, and ski-specific endurance. You'll move faster, react quicker, and build the resilience to handle variable terrain and longer days on the mountain.

Week 8 brings everything together. You'll peak with high-intensity, complex, ski-specific movement, full-body integration, and reactive power. You'll move more efficiently, stay more stable on longer, stronger days on the mountain.

progression.footer: Stronger foundations. Bigger days on snow.

weeks.label: Week 1

weeks.label: Week 4

MONDAY – Single-Leg Power & Lateral Control:

- Reactive control

- Landing mechanics

TUESDAY – Explore & Develop:
- Ski-specific movement exploration
- Light strength or cardio
- Mobility and balance
- Technique work (e.g. hike, lateral movement, cable play, or mobility flow)

WEDNESDAY – Reactive Agility & Off-Balance Loading:
- Multi-directional jumps
- Cable reactive work
- Single-leg stability
- Core integration
- Change of direction

THURSDAY – Explore & Develop:
- Movement variety
- Optional cardio or hike
- Single-leg balance drills
- Mobility and tissue work
- Focus on quality movement (no prescribed sets/reps)

FRIDAY – Total Body Power & Ski-Specific Integration:
- Combined power
- Single-leg & multi-planar
- Core and rotation
- Endurance and control
- Ski-specific patterns

SATURDAY – Mountain Simulation:
- 60-120 min hike or incline walk (Zone 2)
- Uneven terrain
- Longer duration
- Mobility (daily)

SUNDAY – Rest & Recovery:
- Rest
- Optional sauna or cold plunge
- Mobility (light)

KEY FORM CUES:
- Keep knees in line with toes.
- Explode, stick, and control.
- Use your core, not your lower back.
- Keep hips level and stable.
- Land soft and quiet.
- Control the eccentric (lowering).
- Quality over quantity.
- Move with intent, not speed.

sourceNotes: Read 8 sheets (weeks 1-8), each 1024x1536 portrait, from Drive thumbnails at w2400; all present, no duplicates. Layout per sheet: header (MD FIT Performance & Rehab, 'Move better. Play longer.', 'ADVANCED SKI PROGRAM', '8-WEEK PLAN | WEEK n', focus line 'POWER | SINGLE-LEG DOMINANCE | REACTIVE STABILITY', a week-specific intro paragraph, side box 'STRONGER ANKLES. MORE CONTROL. LESS FATIGUE. BIGGER DAYS ON SNOW.'), a 5-item benefits row (dailyBasics), WEEK n SCHEDULE (7 days; Monday/Wednesday/Friday are the three gym workouts, Tuesday/Thursday 'Explore & Develop', Saturday 'Mountain Simulation', Sunday 'Rest & Recovery'; recorded in each week's notes), DAILY MOBILITY ROUTINE (PERFORM EVERY DAY – 10-15 MIN) with 8 items and a focus line, three workout tables (Monday/Wednesday/Friday, 6 rows each, no time boxes), RECOVERY FOCUS (DAILY) with 8 items, KEY FORM CUES (week 1 version = top-level principles; weeks 4-8 print a different 7- or 8-item list, recorded in those weeks' notes), and footer 'STRONGER FOUNDATIONS. BIGGER DAYS ON SNOW.' plus 'GOSD – Glutes on. Shoulders down.' Week 1's schedule has no bullet lists under Monday/Wednesday/Friday and its heading is just 'WEEK 1 SCHEDULE'. Top-level 'goal' is the side box text (no explicit goals box on the sheets); progression.overview holds each week's intro paragraph. Mobility and recovery are identical on all 8 sheets and are repeated as exercises in each week.
